title: Control plane heartbeat loss → tiered shedding and SLO misses (retrospective)
creator: Liam Chen
description: Summary: On 2025-09-12 a control-plane heartbeat loss to the eu-west region controller coincided with an aggressive tiered load-shedding policy. The combination caused sticky regional affinity to be reapplied incorrectly, multiple circuit-breakers to trip asymmetrically, and a cascade of spillback traffic that produced SLO misses for 2.5 hours across EU and NA zones. This retrospective documents timeline, root cause, mitigations, and tracked follow-ups.
timeline: 2025-09-12T03:11Z - First sign: control-plane heartbeat poll for eu-west dropped intermittently; controller logged retries but reported region as 'degraded'
2025-09-12T03:17Z - Autoscaler observed growth in request tails for eu-west and opened tiered shedding window (silver → gold thresholds violated)
2025-09-12T03:20Z - Regional affinity reconciler re-applied 'sticky' routing after perceived unhealthy hosts, moving traffic to other regions
2025-09-12T03:26Z - Circuit breaker hysteresis in secondary regions closed aggressively due to sudden spike; queue backpressure increased
2025-09-12T03:40Z - Spillback loop: failed requests and retries from secondary regions amplified load back to primary control plane and to other regions
2025-09-12T05:45Z - Engineering mitigation: disabled tiered shedding policy for affected customers and temporarily relaxed affinity rebalancing
2025-09-12T06:30Z - Full recovery: control-plane heartbeats restored and circuit-breakers returned to normal thresholds after manual overrides
impact:
- Duration: ~2.5 hours of degraded success rate for generation API in eu-west and elevated tail latency in na-west and eu-central.
- Customer-visible: ~120 customers observed elevated error rates; 14 had automated retries exceed their timeouts and logged user-visible failures.
- SLOs: Token success rate SLO for eu-west slipped from 99.95% to 99.1% during the window; latency p95 doubled for some routes.
root_cause: A sequence of independent protections (control-plane heartbeat detection, sticky regional affinity reapplication, and tiered load-shedding) interacted in an unexpected order. The immediate trigger was a transient packet-loss event between control-plane and eu-west agent group which led the control-plane to mark eu-west as 'degraded'. The degraded marking caused the affinity reconciler to migrate traffic and the shedding policy to aggressively shift capacity; secondary regions then tripped circuit breakers due to spike-shaped fanout and retry amplification. Two systemic design gaps amplified the event: (1) affinity rebalancing lacked a gradual ramp/hysteresis when control-plane health signals oscillate, and (2) circuit-breaker thresholds used absolute queue-length triggers without accounting for short-lived topology shifts, causing asymmetric tripping and spillback.
contributing_factors: No exponential backoff between affinity rebalancer decisions when heartbeat flaps occurred
Shedding policy had identical thresholds for primary and secondary regions rather than region-aware baselines
Circuit-breaker hysteresis windows were too short for topology-change noise and used queue-length rather than stabilized rate estimates
Retry policy on the client-side combined with service-side immediate rejects created amplification loops
Lack of a fast visualization surface in Console to show cross-region spill metrics; on-call had to manually query multiple dashboards
short_term_mitigations: 2025-09-12 (ops): Temporarily disabled tiered shedding for affected customers and reverted affinity rebalancer to conservative mode (Aisha Kaur)
2025-09-12 (ops): Manually widened CB hysteresis windows in secondary regions to prevent immediate trip (on-call)
2025-09-13 (engineering): Deployed improved heartbeat smoothing in control-plane to ignore isolated packet-loss blips (PR #8291)
2025-09-14 (pm): Notified top 20 impacted customers with incident summary and post-incident next steps
long_term_actions: ENG-51783: Implement affinity-rebalancer ramp and exponential backoff for heartbeat flaps; include safety flags for temporary toggles (owner: Aisha Kaur; due: 2025-10-15)
ENG-51784: Region-aware shedding: calibrate thresholds per region using 30d baseline and add a gradual ramp policy (owner: Rajiv Malhotra; due: 2025-11-01)

ENG-51785: Circuit-breaker redesign: move from raw queue-length to stabilized request-rate estimators and add cross-region covariance checks to avoid asymmetric trips (owner: Maya Rivera; due: 2025-11-20)
ENG-52010: Client-side retry alignment: publish recommended retry jitter windows and enforce soft quota for automated retries during region failovers (owner: Developer Relations; due: 2025-10-30)
ENG-52344: Console enhancement: new 'cross-region spill' dashboard and alert to show rejected->retry amplification within 5m buckets (owner: Console team; due: 2025-10-22)
postmortem_notes: Design principle gap: protections that are independently sane can produce unsafe emergent behavior when composed — we must test compositions with fault-injection in the staging multi-region environment.
Operational improvement: add a runbook step to pause affinity rebalancing and shedding together if either control-plane heartbeats or autoscaler signals flip rapidly
We will add a synthetic workload test that introduces transient packet loss on control-plane connections and asserts that no more than X% of traffic migrates in any 10m window
updates: 2025-09-13 - Liam Chen: Confirmed root-cause analysis and merged heartbeat smoothing PR; started tracking long-term engineering tickets.
2025-09-15 - Aisha Kaur: Completed operational playbook update and ran the new manual toggle in a drill; found one UI race condition in the console control.
2025-09-20 - Maya Rivera: Drafted CB redesign proposal; initial internal review requested from SRE and Runtime teams.
2025-09-24 - Rajiv Malhotra: Began calibration job to generate 30d regional baselines for shedding thresholds; job scheduled weekly
